diagram_math_checks.justification: The Statement (lines 26–28) defines nonnegative rate pairs with R1<=C1, R2<=C2 and R1+R2<=S. The figure axes are R1 horizontally and R2 vertically; shading lies in their nonnegative quadrant. The channel supplier fixes Pj>=0 and N>0; no new hypotheses replace those of the theorem.

For P1,P2>0, monotonicity of log gives S>max(C1,C2). Also (1+P1/N)(1+P2/N)=1+(P1+P2)/N+P1*P2/N^2>1+(P1+P2)/N, hence S<C1+C2. Thus 0<S-C1<C2 and 0<S-C2<C1; intersecting the three half-planes gives exactly (0,0),(C1,0),(C1,S-C1),(S-C2,C2),(0,C2). The non-axis edge satisfies R1+R2=S throughout.

With P1=P2=N, C1=C2=C=ln(2)/2 and S=ln(3)/2. Both axes use the same drawing scale 3/C. Thus U has drawing coordinates (3,3*ln(3/2)/ln(2)) and V the reverse; the rendered decimal 1.7548875 differs from the exact latter coordinate by less than 3e-8. U=(C,S-C), V=(S-C,C). Every point of the drawn sloping edge has coordinate sum 4.7548875, representing S to drawing precision.
